6. The learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff f-petitioner submits that the Additional District Judge committed error in law, which resulted in erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice inasmuch as he misconstrued the C.S. and R.S. Khatians which stand in the name of plaintiff-petitioner's predecessor Momin Khan and the fact of payment of rent by plaintiff- petitioner was also not given due consideration. 

 7. The learned Additional District Judge erred in law and fact in holding that petitioner's claim of the suit land being gifted by his after and subsequently by his grandfather has not been proved though evidence was led to that effect and it was not controverted by the defendants. It is further urged by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the lower appellate Court erred in holding that notice under section 87 of the B.T. Act is not necessary while entering the land of a tenant treating the same as abandoned It is further urged that the learned Additional District Judge should have held that mere nonpayment of rent by the tenant does not extinguish the tenancy. 

 11. As per provision of section 87 of B.T. Act, rayot or under rayoti can voluntarily abandon residence without notice to his landlord and without arranging for payment of rent, the landlord may at any time after expiration of agricultural year in which the rayoit or under rayoit so abandoned and ceased to cultivate enters on the holding and lets it to another tenant or takes into cultivation to himself sub-section 2 of section 87 contemplates that before a landlord enters under section 87 he shall file a notice on the prescribed form in the collector's office stating that he has treated the holding to be abandoned and is about to enter on it accordingly and the collector shall cause a notice to be published in the prescribed manner. But there is absolutely no evidence to show if any such notice was give to the collector's office treating the suit land as a abandoned property. What constitutes an abandonment is a question of fact depending upon the circumstances of each case. Legislature has laid down 3 guiding factors for determination of the question of abandonment. 

 (2) Does not arrange for payment of rent as it falls due. 

 13. Further it appears that series of dakhilas have been filed by the plaintiff-petitioner to prove payment of rent. 

 15. The other document which is of much importance is the copy of compensation assesemant roll prepared in the name of the defendant's ex-landlord. It has been marked as Ext. 4. It purports to show compensation assessment roll for the rent receiving interest was prepared in the name of the defendant's landlord and this preparation of compensation assessment in the name of defendants' predecessor enough to prove that compensation was duly awarded to the predecessors of defendants. 

 16. Thus, having regard to entry in C.S. and R.S. records of right standing in the name of original owner Momin Khan and payment of rent upto year 1383 B.S. On production of series of dhakhilas (Ext. 2 series) and the preparation of assessment roll in the name of predecessor of defendant opposite parties (vide Ext. 4) and absence of evidence about alleged abandonment, the 1st appellate Court committed error in law having failed to consider the relevant document referred above.
